What to look for in waterproof jackets

  • Laminated beats drop-liner. A bonded waterproof membrane keeps the outer from soaking through and chilling you in sustained rain.
  • CE Level 2 armour. Insist on shoulder and elbow protectors, and budget for a back protector if one is not included.
  • Layering system. A removable thermal liner turns one jacket into a three-season solution for British weather.
  • Connection zip. A jacket-to-trouser zip stops your kit separating in a slide — buy matching pieces where possible.

Frequently asked questions

How much should I spend on waterproof jackets?

Our catalogue spans £119.99 to £1,240. Budget options under £150 cover the essentials, the £150–£400 mid-range hits the sweet spot for most UK tourers, and premium picks above £400 add refinement, lighter materials and longer-term durability.

Which brands are worth considering?

Popular, well-reviewed brands in this category include Klim, Rev'it, Alpinestars. All are stocked by SportsBikeShop with UK warranty support.

Textile or leather?

Textile is the practical all-weather choice for UK touring thanks to waterproof membranes and thermal liners. Leather offers the best abrasion resistance for spirited, dry-weather sport touring. Many riders own both.

faq.q: What makes a jacket genuinely waterproof?
faq.a: The key is a bonded waterproof and breathable membrane such as Gore-Tex or Alpinestars Drystar, laminated to the outer shell so the fabric cannot soak up water. Taped seams and water-resistant zips complete the seal. Cheaper jackets place the membrane as a separate inner liner, which works but lets the outer wet out, holding water and chilling you.

faq.q: Is Gore-Tex worth the extra money?
faq.a: Gore-Tex laminates, used on the Klim Badlands Pro and Carlsbad and the Rev'it Vertical, offer the most reliable long-term waterproofing and breathability, backed by a strong guarantee. They command a premium. Alpinestars Drystar jackets like the Bogota Pro and Andes V4 deliver excellent real-world waterproofing for far less, so they are a smart pick if the top-tier budget is out of reach.

faq.q: Will a waterproof jacket be too hot in summer?
faq.a: A fully waterproof shell traps more heat than a mesh jacket, but the better options include zipped or waterproof vents that let you dump heat when moving. For genuinely hot, dry days many riders prefer a dedicated mesh jacket. For the typical changeable UK forecast, a vented laminated jacket is the more versatile single choice.

faq.q: How do I keep a waterproof jacket performing?
faq.a: The membrane keeps working, but the outer face fabric relies on a durable water repellent (DWR) coating that wears off over time, causing the surface to soak and look like it is leaking. Wash the jacket with a technical cleaner and reproof it with a spray-on or wash-in DWR treatment, then reactivate it with gentle heat. This restores water beading and breathability.

faq.q: Do I still need separate over-trousers?
faq.a: A waterproof jacket only covers your top half, so pair it with waterproof trousers or a laminated riding trouser to stay fully dry. Look for a connection zip so the two link together. Many riders match a laminated jacket with laminated trousers from the same range, avoiding the faff of pulling waterproofs over your kit at the roadside.
